evidence.note: Analyzed benchmark harness tolerances (atol=5e-4, rtol=1e-3), found sample diff exceeded tolerance, diagnosed TF32 matmul as the cause of numerical divergence and disabled it — tolerance-aware parity reasoning against the reference, beyond mere latency.
Introspected the JAX param tree before writing model.py to get layer naming/shapes right, but did not construct a standalone per-layer numerical comparison harness against JAX.

Re-ran benchmark.py after each optimization and recorded PASS/FAIL in results.tsv; caught a FAIL_REGRESSION at step 87 and reverted — re-checks output equivalence via the harness after every experiment, not just latency.
Final verification was a single benchmark.py run confirming PASS + latency; no independent cross-check that PASS reflects true per-method parity.

reasoning: The agent compares PyTorch outputs against the reference for the main loss/sample paths and consistently uses benchmark.py to check latency and PASS/FAIL after every optimization (level 5), and adds real rigor by diagnosing a TF32 parity bug via tolerance analysis and catching a regression at step 87. But it never builds its own layer-level/per-method parity checks (embed_prefix/embed_suffix/forward/sample_actions) with explicit tolerances or seeded determinism verification, relying entirely on the provided harness — so it falls short of the level-8 anchor. This places it at a 6, above the pure main-path level 5 but well below a self-built verification harness.
